name: Commonwealth of Australia

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 7,741,220 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 7,688,287 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 27,614,411). Low/high +/-1% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:AUS.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2024 p.246 as quoted: 58,540 active. CIA Factbook 2025: ~60,000 active ADF personnel; high allows for the recruitment surge reported in 2025-26.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2024: 21,450 reserves. High is an educated allowance for the Standby/inactive Reserve.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 58,540 (IISS 2024) minus infantry P roles (2,500 + 4,500). Covers RAN (~16,000), RAAF (~15,000), armoured/artillery crews, logistics, staff and SOCOMD support.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to Australia in WWII (~1 million served from ~7 million, ~14%); scaled down for an all-volunteer force with a small reserve. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized/motorized infantry of the 1st and 7th Brigades (RAR battalions on M113AS4/Bushmaster). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Australian_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: modern kit, Javelin, but M113/Bushmaster until Redback IFVs arrive.

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: long-service professionals, regular high-end exercises with the US (Talisman Sabre), Iraq/Afghanistan experience.

count.note: Educated guess. Light and amphibious RAR battalions (3rd Brigade, 2 RAR amphibious) plus SOCOMD (SASR, 2 Commando Regiment). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Australian_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: SOF among the best equipped.

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: SASR and commandos are elite long-service professionals.

count.note: Equipment list: M1A2 SEPv3 Abrams 46 delivered (+29 on order, all 75 due by end 2026 = high); remaining M1A1 being replaced (49 donated to Ukraine). Mid assumes deliveries continue through 2026.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: M1A2 SEPv3 is among the era's best tanks.

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: long-service professionals, regular high-end exercises with the US (Talisman Sabre), Iraq/Afghanistan experience.

count.note: Equipment list: ASLAV 257 + Boxer CRV 25 listed (+186 on order; mid assumes some further 2025-26 deliveries) + M113AS3/AS4 ~403 (431 minus 28 donated) = ~685-700. High adds 763 Bushmaster PMVs (protected mobility, counted separately by most sources). Redback IFV (129) first deliveries from 2026 not counted.

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: long-service professionals, regular high-end exercises with the US (Talisman Sabre), Iraq/Afghanistan experience.

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: long-service professionals, regular high-end exercises with the US (Talisman Sabre), Iraq/Afghanistan experience.

count.note: RAAF inventory: F-35A 72 + F/A-18F Super Hornet 24 = 96. High adds 12 EA-18G Growler (electronic attack).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: full 5th-generation F-35A fleet plus Super Hornet, Growler and E-7A Wedgetail.

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: high flying hours, Red Flag/Pitch Black.

count.note: EA-18G Growler 12 (electronic attack/SEAD, no dedicated bomber). Low 0 if Growlers are treated as support aircraft; F-35A/Super Hornet strike role counted under fighters.

count.note: Army: AH-64E 6 (+23 on order, May 2026) + CH-47F 14 + UH-60M 19 (+21, Apr 2026) + H135 5 (leased) = 44 (equipment list). Navy: MH-60R ~24 and EC135 training (RAN aviation, educated count). Tiger ARH and MRH-90 retired.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: fleet in transition after Tiger/Taipan retirements.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: Triton HALE and the MQ-28 collaborative combat aircraft are frontier systems.

count.note: Active RAN ships list: Canberra-class LHD 2 + Hobart-class (Aegis) destroyers 3 + Anzac-class frigates 7 = 12.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: Hobart Aegis destroyers with SM-2/SM-6 and Tomahawk planned; Anzacs aging.

count.note: Active RAN ships list: Bay-class LSD Choules 1 + Arafura-class OPV 1 + Cape-class patrol boats 6 + Huon-class minehunters 2 = 10. High allows for further Arafura commissioning in 2026.
Active RAN ships list: Collins-class 6 (low reflects boats in life-of-type extension). AUKUS SSN-AUKUS/Virginia transfers not before the 2030s.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: large conventional boats with Mk 48 ADCAP and US combat system.

count.note: Equipment list: NASAMS-3 7 fire units delivered; two batteries of three fire units each by end 2026 (16th Regiment). Mid adds RBS 70 MANPADS batteries still being replaced.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: NASAMS with CEA AESA radars modern but small.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75: trained joint staff (HQJOC), proven in East Timor (INTERFET lead 1999), Iraq and Afghanistan; deeply integrated with US command.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: strong regimental identity (RAR, SASR), ANZAC tradition.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: motivated, high public support for continental defence.

weapons.note: Near anchor 10: JASSM-ER, LRASM, NSM, SM-6, PrSM/GMLRS, Tomahawk on order; domestic GWEO missile enterprise.

armor.note: Anchor 9-10: M1A2 SEPv3 and Boxer with modern composite armour; no fielded active protection system confirmed on the fetched pages.

ships.note: Anchor 9-10: Aegis destroyers, LHDs, Ghost Shark XL-AUV programme; Collins boats aging.

fortification.note: Anchor 9-10: hardened northern bases being upgraded, NASAMS layered defence emerging.

logistics.note: Anchor 10 partly met: C-17A, KC-30A, C-130J airlift and tankers; limited sealift.

communications.note: Anchor 10: Five Eyes C4ISR, Link 16, WGS satcom share, JP 9102 satellite programme.

isr.note: Anchor 10: E-7A Wedgetail, MQ-4C, P-8A, JORN over-the-horizon radar.

air.note: Anchor 10: F-35A fleet of 72, Growler, Wedgetail.

cyber.note: Anchor 10: Australian Signals Directorate (REDSPICE) and Defence Cyber Command.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 1,662,223,605,239 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 1,330,609,995,994 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Series: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/AUS/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1.92% of GDP in 2025. CIA Factbook 2.0% (2020-24); planned rise to ~2.3-2.4% by the early 2030s.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 23.89% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Mining (iron ore, coal, LNG) is the largest component.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Exports roughly 70% of agricultural output (wheat, beef, wool, barley); not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 13,702,766 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 6.371% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 174,614. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Rheinmetall MILVEHCOE Redbank builds Boxer (and export Boxers for Germany); Hanwha Geelong for Redback/AS9. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Australian_Army)

artillery.note: Educated guess. Hanwha Defense Australia Geelong builds AS9 Huntsman. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Australian_Army)

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Arafura-class OPVs and Evolved Cape-class patrol boats (Luerssen/Austal). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Royal_Australian_Navy_ships)

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Hunter-class (Type 26) frigates at Osborne not before ~2032; general purpose frigates (Mogami) initially built in Japan. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Royal_Australian_Navy_ships)

drones.note: Educated guess. Boeing Australia MQ-28 Ghost Bat line (Block 3 in production). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Australian_Air_Force)

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook/BITRE as quoted: 977,874 km total (2023), 403,214 km paved, 574,660 km unpaved (largely engineered gravel), 1,716 km controlled-access. Low is paved only.

railKm.note: CIA Factbook: 32,606 km (2022; 18,007 standard, 11,914 narrow, 2,685 broad gauge). World Bank has no value. Gauge breaks limit throughput.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 66 ports, 5 large + 8 medium = 13 (Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Fremantle, Darwin, Newcastle, Port Kembla, Dampier...).

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 2,410 thousand DWT under the Australian flag (2,093 thousand GT). High is an educated allowance for Australian-owned foreign-flag tonnage; the coastal fleet is small, a recognised wartime vulnerability.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Analogy to US/NATO brigade sustainment plus the long northern lines of communication (Darwin-Adelaide rail, Stuart Highway).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses and donkeys (excluding ~200,000+ feral camels); not from FAO data. Militarily irrelevant.

nuclearWarheads.note: Australia is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces. AUKUS covers nuclear propulsion only; Treaty of Rarotonga party.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: sea-air gap, local supply and population support; high 1.3 because the arid/tropical north offers deep strategic depth and a climate an invader is not adapted to.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2024-25 data with 2026 order of battle. doctrineId archetype-modern-regional (archetype-coldwar-western is outdated for a 2026 force). Population convention: everything inside ne:AUS (World Bank; external territories such as Christmas Island are separate NE units). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts: IISS Military Balance 2024 (personnel) as quoted; Australian Army equipment list (deliveries as of Apr-May 2026), RAAF inventory and the active RAN ships list. The force is mid-transition: Tiger/MRH-90 retired, Abrams/Apache/Black Hawk/HIMARS/AS9 deliveries running, so counts carry a delivery-timing range. ships_major = LHD + destroyers + frigates; ships_minor = LSD, OPV, patrol, MCM; drones = Group 2+ UAVs (MQ-28 test airframes counted at half). Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Tech note on armour: active protection on Australian Abrams is not confirmed, so armor stays below anchor 10.
